questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Great academic opportunities at big well-known university. Just as much the opportunity to live in a different culture, in a great location with nice weather, nature and things to do and see.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Would for sure have rated higher if exchange wasn't so affected by the covid situation.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: fairly easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: E-mails from UCEAP regarding important and necessary steps.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very disappointed that UCEAP/UCLA didn't do anything in order to "welcome" us internationals and get us to know each other, or nothing at all...

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy. Don't be picky. Don't sign or pay anything before you have inspected the property, as there are many scammers. Make a handfull of appointments at different places prior going to LA. Get to LA early an inspect the homes. There are many facebook pages for housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Nice not sharing room with 1-2 people. Possible to find cheaper accommodation as well. But a bit annoying commuting to campus everyday, for socials/school.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Was offered a bunkbed in a triple room for 1500$, with no meals or anything included. Insane.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Process was simple enough, but we weren't provided with any info. We had to find out everything on our own. Also, as exchange students you have no pre-reqs in the system and hence you´ll need instructor consent to enroll. We weren't informed about this as well, and as a result I got 0 of my desired courses the first quarter, as courses fill up quickly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Enrollments appts. app 2-3 weeks before quarter start. add/drop period first 2 weeks of quarter where you can see if the courses are of interest or if you want something else instead.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much. Research on you own a UCLA website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unsuccesful first quarter due to before mentioned reasons. Very succesfull 2nd quarter. Also, you can get graduate courses even though you're not grad. E-mail the professor, be polite and argue why you are eligible and why you want the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find courses in good time before enrollment apts. and e-mail the instructor about enrollment so you're ready when enrollment starts.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Would probably rate higher if not for covid and a lot of remote instruction. Thought the level would have been higher though, but it wasn't higher than at university of Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level varied a lot. Did both undergrad and grad courses. But in general I think undergrads are a bit to slowly progressing in the course, and a bit too basic... felt a bit like highschoolclasses at times.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Here there was a lot more lectures. I'm used to quite a lot of practical lab work as well. Also, there's a lot of hand-in assignments, midterms every third weeks and a lot of things getting graded all the time. Even though the level is definitely not higher than in Denmark, its a lot more stressful here.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
2 quarters, not 2 semesters.
MCDB144: Molecular biology of cellular processes 
Neurosc M101A: From Molecules to Mind-Cellular and Systems Neuroscience
Neuro M202: Cellular Neurophysiology

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Physci 241: Neural Plasticity and Repair
Neurosc M101B: From molecules to mind - molecular and developmental neuroscience
Neuro 205: Systems neuroscience

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked M202 and 205 a lot. Stay away from m101a.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There was a bunch of different administrative extra fees to UCLA (200$).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was more expensive than I imagined. Everything is more expensive than in Denmark. Especially decent normal healthy groceries are 2-3x danish prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great selection of different clubs that you can join from, and they held big events where you could go check out if it was of interest. The sport facilities at UCLA are also amazing! Its possible to do whatever sport you want.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would believe there is a club/organization for whatever you need.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Join some sport clubs. There are all sports at all levels. Great way to meet new people. also the hike club as california has a lot of beatiful nature and the club arrange trips at very favorable prices and with great people. 
If your´e undergrad an into it, try joining a frat. Seems like a lot of fun, but I unfortunately felt a bit too "old" for that, especially because american students are pretty young..

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Lot of stuff to do in LA on weekends if you haven't got time or money for bigger trips; Santa Monica, Venice, down town, Basket, american football, hollywood, griffith observatory, universal, Disney, Getty center and other museums. 
Whenever you have the chance you should visit other cities and nature spots in Cali; San Diego, Drive along the coast to San Francisco and see all the nice stuff on the way. Napa, Death Valley, Yosemite, Tahoe. Also visit Vegas, its pretty close to LA, and drop by Grand Canyon when there as its close to Vegas.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs that interests you. People are in general more friendly and open compared to Scandinavians, so pretty easy to meet new people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: LA is a car city. Its not made for cyclists. It was okay getting around between Venice, Santa Monica and campus on bike. But its impossible seeing the rest of the city on bike, because of the distances but more because that infrastructure is made for cars. Also public transport was bad, and not safe after dark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were very open and friendly compared to home. It was much easier to engage and make new connections.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be openminded and you will have no problem making new friends.
Try not to get caught up in the "grading-culture" at Uni. People take their grades extremely serious. Enjoy your stay and get some nice experiences instead. 
Be open and do whatever you find interesting, its a once in lifetime opportunity!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Compared to the other UC´s this is more academic focused, and you will probably work more here compared to in San Diego or Santa Barbara. So if you are going on exchange mainly to have fun and enjoy life, choose these instead.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I went on my own, not knowing a single person before I arrived. I had to be very open and seek out people myself, and I think I learned a lot socially from this.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was really hard accepting how money vanished at an insane rate:( Very expensive

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
